Cc: contracts@clearpay.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: unusual transaction loss observed 2028-06-15

Hi David,

We started seeing a stream of failed checkout confirmations around 08:58 PDT this morning; roughly a 2.1% uplift in failed transactions for a 23-minute window. Our side shows successful tokenization but Redwood calls returned 502/503 intermittently — several orders were dropped rather than queued. Can you validate the exact window where Redwood observed elevated error rate and confirm whether this qualifies as an availability incident under our contract (SLO: 99.95% monthly availability for the inference endpoint)?

We need the validated window and a preliminary assessment of compensation path (pro-rata credit vs. fixed remedy) — legal and finance are on standby. I attached a small sample of transaction IDs and your request-id headers.

Thanks,
Sophia
Head of Payments Operations
ClearPay

Attachments: sample_ids.csv (csv)

Hi Sophia — thanks for flagging and for the sample IDs. We're escalating this to infra and SRE now. Initial ask: can you confirm the top-level endpoint (region/us-west-2) and whether the failing calls were hitting a single route (charge.submit) or multiple routes? That will help narrow routing vs. model-instance issues.

We will:
- Pull an availability timeline (per-minute success/error rate) for the timeframe you reported
- Collect trace-level request-ids and matching server-side traces
- Share a list of affected shard/pod IDs if preemption or eviction occurred

I included Laura (CS lead) and Ben (SRE on-call) to coordinate log bundle and a quick mitigation plan. We'll aim to get a validated window and a telemetry bundle by EOD today.

—David
David Kim
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 11:05:33 -07:00
Subject: Re: unusual transaction loss observed 2028-06-15

Quick status update from infra: we saw a cluster-level autoscaler churn in us-west-2 at 08:56:42 PDT causing 12 short-lived pod restarts across the inference pool for the payment endpoint. Error spike aligns closely with 08:56:30–09:19:00 PDT (26.5 minutes) on our aggregates. Root cause appears to be a scheduler regression that mis-evaluated node resource pressure after a recent kernel update; several pods were preempted and not warmed quickly enough.

I'll attach the raw traces and the token-level error histogram. Preliminary eligibility: this looks like a sustained availability impact that would exceed the per-request error baseline in the SLO. We should collect the conservative overlap window with ClearPay's reported failures and prepare a proportional remedy estimate.

Attachments: transaction_logs_20280615.zip (log bundle), clearpay_trace_bundle.ndjson (filtered traces)

—Ben
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sophia Allen <sophia.allen@clearpay.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, contracts@clearpay.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 13:34:07 -07:00
Subject: Transaction loss window validation and next steps

Hi Sophia,

Thanks for the patience — we validated telemetry and aligned windows. Our conservative validated impact window is 2028-06-15T08:56:30Z through 2028-06-15T09:22:00Z (UTC timestamps converted below). That corresponds to ~26.5 minutes where server-side error rate exceeded the SLO threshold for your endpoint in us-west-2.

What we are offering as next steps:
1) Evidence bundle (attached): per-request traces, token histograms, pod restart events, and an aggregated availability timeline.
2) Compensation calculation: per-contract remedy is pro-rata credit based on lost successful requests. Preliminary estimate: 0.44% of that day's invoice for the affected route; we will produce the exact credit calculation by Monday after cross-checking your billing window and de-duplication of any client-side retries.
3) Post-incident plan: a short RCA draft and mitigation actions (scheduler rollback and node prioritization rules) — Ben will lead technical write-up; I'll coordinate distribution and a follow-up sync.

Can you confirm:
- Which billing window you want us to align the credit to (UTC midnight or your local billing cycle)?
- Any additional artifacts you need for legal/finance (signed waiver, DocuSign link)?

I've attached the telemetry and included a provisional DocuSign link for the credit agreement form if that route is preferred.

Laura Bennett
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: signed-terms-ClearPay-CP-4721.pdf, DocuSign: https://docusign.com/abc123
From: Sophia Allen <sophia.allen@clearpay.com>

Date: Sun, 17 Jun 2028 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Transaction loss window validation and next steps

Hi Laura — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the conservative window. We confirm ClearPay wants the credit aligned to our UTC billing day (midnight UTC). Please proceed with the pro-rata calculation and include the de-duped transaction set (we have a handful of retries that should not be double counted).

Two asks before you finalize:
- Can Ben include a short note on whether any cached inference state (KV cache) could have caused undercounts for customer retries? We need assurance retries weren't swallowed at the cache layer.
- Please open a ticket that includes the HubSpot record HSP-987654 and our internal PO reference PO-CP-2219 so finance can track the credit.

If possible, we'll sign the DocuSign credit form after we reconcile numbers; finance needs the ticket id for their ledger.

Regards,
Sophia
Head of Payments Operations, ClearPay
